chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a said, and Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"A man died and left behind a brother who was a slave, and he bequeathed to him one thousand dirhams. His masters refused to validate this for him, so they appealed to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. He said to the slave: 'Do you have children?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Are they free?' He said: 'They are free.'"
He said: 'Do you accept from all the wealth only one thousand dirhams, so that they inherit their uncle?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz was correct.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave inheriting from a free relative according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the juristic principle of 'al-walad li-al-mawla' (the child follows the status of the master), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz’s ruling that a slave’s bequest benefits his free offspring, thereby preserving the inheritance rights of the free uncle. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding mixed-status families and the acceptance of sound legal reasoning even from non-imams when it aligns with divine law.
